holidays.name: World Vegan Day
holidays.description: Plant-based eaters and the plant-curious get together on November 1. They swap recipes, try dairy-free versions of favorite foods, and show that a meal can be tasty without any animal products.
holidays.origin: Louise Wallis, then chair of The Vegan Society in the UK, started it in 1994. It marked the 50th anniversary of the Society, which was founded in 1944. It has since become a global celebration.
holidays.funFact: The word 'vegan' was coined in 1944 by Donald Watson, co-founder of The Vegan Society. He built it from the first and last letters of 'vegetarian'.

holidays.name: National Vinegar Day
holidays.description: This day is for the sour, tangy liquid that lives in your pantry. Pickle some vegetables, whip up a vinaigrette, or clean your windows with it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a pantry-staple favorite on the food holiday calendar.
holidays.funFact: The word 'vinegar' comes from the French 'vin aigre', meaning 'sour wine'. Vinegar has been made for thousands of years, and traces of it have been found in ancient Egyptian jars.

holidays.name: National Calzone Day
holidays.description: A day for the pizza's folded-over cousin. The dough is stuffed with melty cheese, sauce and your favorite fillings, then baked until golden.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. The food it celebrates comes from Naples, Italy, where it was created as a handheld, portable take on pizza.
holidays.funFact: 'Calzone' is Italian for 'trouser leg' or 'pant leg'. The name is thought to come from the stuffed pocket's resemblance to one.
